column1: # boru Language Specification: Value reads (valof / /v)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# valof name → resolve a name to its bound VALUE, disabling any call the
#              name would induce. Companion to the `/v` word suffix.
# name/v     → the same operation as a suffix.
# `valof` and `/v` are ONE operation and must behave identically in every
# position. A bare reference is INERT at the reference site: it is left on
# the stack as an (unquoted) Function value and is never auto-invoked —
# not even a 0-arg fn. The SAME value dispatches normally when it is
# re-stepped elsewhere: unwrapped from a paren, retrieved from a map slot,
# or handed to `apply`.
# `valof` is TOTAL over every binding kind: for a fn binding it suppresses
# the call, and for any other binding it is the identity. There is no
# function-only gate — that totality is the point, because it is what
# lets ONE spelling read a slot whose kind is not known statically
# (NUR085, resolved by this rule). The only refusal left is an UNBOUND
# name, which has no value to take: [boru/undefined_word].
# §1  Bare reference is inert (held) — `valof` ≡ `/v`, no auto-fire
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  z/v
column3: bare /v holds a 0-arg fn — NOT fired

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  valof z
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (inc/v)
column3: a held reference is a Function value

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (valof inc)
# §2  The held value dispatches when RE-STEPPED (paren unwrap)
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  (z/v)
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  (valof z)
column3: valof fires when re-stepped — same as /v

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  (inc/v) 5
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  (valof inc) 5
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (sub2/v) 10 3
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (valof sub2) 10 3
# §3  Reference stored in a map slot dispatches via dot-access
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def ops {f: inc/v}  ops.f 5
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def ops {f: (valof inc)}  ops.f 5
column3: valof in a map slot dispatches

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def ops {f: z/v}  (ops.f)
column3: a 0-arg /v in a map slot courtesy-dispatches on the read (break 2: compiled as an arity-0 dyn-method apply)

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def ops {f: z/v}  ops.f
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def ops {f: z/v}  (ops get f/q) add 1
column3: the get spelling of the same 0-arg read, consumed downstream

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def lst [z/v]  (lst get 0)
column3: a 0-arg /v in a LIST slot courtesy-dispatches by concrete index

column1: # §4  Reference handed to `apply` (stack form: args... fn/v apply)
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc/v apply
column3: apply invokes a referenced fn against stack args

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/v apply
column3: apply on a 2-arg referenced fn (stack order)

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  z/v apply
# §5  Anonymous-function references behave identically
def f [a:Integer b:Integer] => [a sub b]  typeof (f/v)
def f n:Integer => [n add 1]  (f/v) 5
def f n:Integer => [n add 1]  5 f/v apply

column3: a lambda inside a list is held, never fired in place

column1: # §6  Negatives — the ONLY refusal is a name with nothing bound to it.
#     There is no function-only gate: on a non-fn binding both surfaces
#     are the identity, which §9 pins in full.
def x 5  x/v
column3: /v on a non-fn binding is the value itself

column1: def x 5  valof x
column3: valof on a non-fn binding, likewise

column1: nope/v
valof nope
# §7  A `/v`-marked word feeds forward collection as its REFERENCE
#     value (NUR050 fix): it is not a function-word barrier, so it
#     resolves directly as another word's forward argument. (This
#     retired the historical gotcha where `typeof inc/v` stranded with
#     a signature_error and had to be grouped as `typeof (inc/v)`.)
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof inc/v
column3: bare /v resolves as a forward arg (was the grouping gotcha)

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (inc/v)
# §8  A fn body's RETURN is delivered, not re-used
#     A frame collapsing to a single Function value hands it back; the
#     frame's own collapse is not a fresh use of it, so it is not invoked
#     there. This is the ParkResult idiom (`valof`'s own mechanism) applied
#     to the frame result, and it is POSITIONAL — nothing is stamped on
#     the value, so the returned reference still dispatches at its next
#     use (§3 map slot, §4 apply both still hold).
#     Before this, `[f/v]` returned the CALL'S RESULT (7) rather than the
#     function — /v silently doing the opposite of what it says.
#     The argument is handed over with `/v` because passing a function as an
#     argument requires it; a bare name is a call.
#     NOT pinned here: what a USER paren does to such a return. `((h z/v))`
#     is an open interpreter/compiler divergence (interp 42, compiled the fn
#     value) — the §2 re-step rule it turns on is itself under revision, so
#     there is no oracle to pin it against, in this corpus or the frontier
#     one. Recorded as NUR073 (Pending) so the gap is not mistaken for
#     coverage; reasoning in design/FUNCTION-VALUE-SCOPE.0.md §12.6. Do not
#     add a row for it until clause 3 is ruled.
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def h fn [[f:Function][Any][f/v]]  typeof (h z/v)
column3: a /v'd param returned from a body is the fn, not its result

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def h fn [[][Any][z/v]]  typeof (h)
column3: same for a module-scope name — not param-specific

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def h fn [[f:Function][Any][f/v]]  typeof (h inc/v)
# §9  valof is TOTAL — every binding kind, not just functions (NUR085)
#     The negative twin is §10: an unbound name still refuses.
def answer 42  answer/v
column3: /v on an Integer binding is the value itself

column1: def answer 42  valof answer
column3: valof on an Integer binding, likewise

column1: def greet 'hi'  greet/v
def xs [1 2 3]  xs/v
def m {a:1}  m/v
def t true  t/v
def answer 42  typeof (answer/v)
column3: the value keeps its own type — /v does not wrap it

column1: def answer 42  add 1 (answer/v)
column3: and it composes as an ordinary value

column1: # §9b the polymorphic read: ONE body spelling serves both kinds. This is
#     the shape that had no spelling before — `[t]` calls a fn-bound
#     param and `[t/v]` used to refuse a non-fn one.
def idf t:Any => [t/v]  (idf 5)
def idf t:Any => [t/v]  (idf 'x')
def idf t:Any => [t/v]  def g (idf (z:Integer => [add 1 z]))  (g 5)
column3: the same body, a Function — returned uncalled, then applied

column1: def idf t:Any => [t/v]  typeof (idf (z:Integer => [z]))
column3: and it is the Function itself, not its result

column1: # §10  negatives — totality over KINDS is not totality over everything
def answer 42  nope/v
column3: an unbound name has no value to take

column1: def answer 42  valof nope
add/vq
column3: q still cannot combine with v

column1: add/vv
